title: Generate One Campaign in Five Ad Sizes with the Prisma Design API (Node.js)
summary:
A single ad rarely ships alone. The same offer usually needs a square post, a portrait feed version, a full-screen story, a landscape video frame and a link-ad banner. In my previous tutorial we made one Prisma generation: submit, poll, fetch the template and load it into Fabric.js. This time we run a whole campaign: one brief, five aspect ratios, five editable templates on disk.

Five jobs bring new problems: staying inside the rate limits, surviving a dropped connection without paying twice, and knowing which size failed and why. The script below handles all three, then copies the image assets to your own server.

What we're building

Each of Prisma's five aspect ratios is a separate generation. You send the same brief five times with a different aspect_ratio, and Prisma builds a new layout for each canvas

title: Fender serial number lookup in JavaScript: why E412345 can mean the USA or Japan
summary:
Type E412345 into a Fender serial decoder. When and where was the guitar made?

According to Fender's own dating charts, it's one of two guitars:

  • USA, 1984 to 1988. "E4 + 5 digits" is a row on the American chart.
  • Japan, 1984 to 1987. "E + 6 digits" is a row on the Japanese chart.

Both patterns match the same seven characters. The serial alone can't decide. What decides is printed right next to it: the decal that says Made in USA or Made in Japan.

I built a Fender serial number lookup for Who Actually Makes. Every rule in it comes from Fender's support articles, and the build checks every rule against a saved copy of those articles.
